title: Design lineage envelope — one record's whole version chain (GET .../lineage, both id-scoped forms)
description: Four ledger rows read a version chain and said nothing about themselves: the project-scoped brief and direction lineage, and their id-addressed twins under `/api/design-briefs` and `/api/design-directions`. Measured 2026-10-23 against a live boot, the document is `{lineage: {<id_of_the_subject>, root_id, requested_id, live_id, versions[]}}` — and it carries NO event rows. The debt text this file replaces claimed 'the superseded_by chain plus design_layer_event rows': `src/design_lab/design_layer.py` `_chain()` reads `design_layer_event` to find each row's PARENT (the `*-revised` payloads map new_id to old_id), then serves records, not events. That claim was wrong and is corrected here rather than left in a prose field. The four honesty properties this binds are the ones the emitter already implements: `versions` is oldest-first and includes the row that was asked for (`requested_id`), `root_id` is reached by walking parents so any member of the chain resolves to the same lineage, and `live_id` names the current tip explicitly because `version` alone cannot say it — the ACTIVE-version rule of this state store means several rows can hold content and only `superseded_by IS NULL` is current. `subject_kind` is required and must agree with which key the subject id uses, so a brief chain cannot be served under a direction heading. Record shapes are `$ref`'d from their owners: `brief-readback.schema.json` `$defs.brief` and `design-record-v1.schema.json` `$defs.direction`.
